rv.q: I can’t overstate my respect for the show; it’s a masterpiece of its populist kind, much imitated but never equalled.
It's a feast for your pleasure centers.
Those impervious to the band or “Mamma Mia!” should just accept that here is not where the story ends.
Well, joyous if you’re a Mamma Mia! fan, more strenuous if you’re not, and by now it seems likely that everyone knows to which group they belong.
I would not discourage anyone interested from attending Mamma Mia!.
This show, the mother of all jukebox musicals, is nothing if not familiar—and in this case, familiarity breeds contentment.
The ABBA-scored musical is escapist, feather-light entertainment that still delivers on its 20-plus-year promise of pure fun.
This two-and-a-half-hour respite from the world is what we all need right now.
And as this perfectly adequate revival proves, that success is entirely about presenting delightful songs in an attractive, form-fitting package.
The show is pure sunshine baked into a musical and dressed in disco balls, sequins, and feathered boas.
Thank you for the music, indeed!

Theater: Winter Garden Theatre Tickets: Ticketmaster.com Nothing succeeds like success. And so it is with Mamma Mia!, whose initial Broadway outing began at this same theater in 2001 and, with a change in venue to the Broadhurst Theatre for its final two years, stayed around for a total of 14 years and close to 5,800 performances.
Personally, I found this "Mamma Mia" at its most exciting at the curtain call.
Rather, this new production can be described in two words: severely cheapened.
As for the more side of this event, its highly enthusiastic company tends to put the broad in Broadway performing.
Bar a few numbers and its get-up-and-dance finale, the show almost does ABBA down.
Frankly, the show looks so tacky that it could be the original 2001 production with a not-very-good paint job.
Mamma Mia! still has the power to connect with audiences in an old-fashioned, almost primal way.

cn.t: Critics find this feel-good ABBA jukebox musical an irresistible crowd-pleaser despite its flimsy plot and shameless song shoehorning. The infectious disco hits and escapist fun override reservations about the show's artistic merit.

vr.q: Overall, I love this show. I think it's so much fun, and I think it knows exactly what it wants to be.
this production delivers exactly what you'd expect. It's fun, silly, fast moving, full of catchy songs. If you already know you like MMA Mia, this is a great time to see it again.
